\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{x}^{-3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{-3+1}}{-3+1}{|}_{1}^{2} \\  & =-\frac{{x}^{-2}}{2}{|}_{1}^{2} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}({2}^{-2}-{1}^{-2}) \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}(\frac{1}{4}-1) \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}(-\frac{3}{4}) \\  & =\frac{3}{8}.\end{aligned}

e-411.knowledge_point: Evaluating the Definite Integral of a Radical Function
e-411.worked_solution:

$$

after.worked_solution:
Taking the antiderivative and evaluating the difference at the bounds, we get

$$
